title: Market probe: signal ops & competitive telemetry brief
creator: Aria Chen
description:
Objective: Produce a concise, operational brief for product, research, and GTM that standardizes how we collect and react to competitive model availability and performance signals across regions. The brief should enable rapid decisions (route-to-hosted, fallback to dedicated/private, or customer outreach) and include: 1) canonical telemetry metrics, 2) prioritized data sources, 3) lightweight alerting thresholds, 4) recommended investigatory play flows for on-call and PMs, and 5) a short experiment plan for validating signal quality.

Why now: Multiple customers in EMEA/APAC reported intermittent degradation when model variants shifted providers or quantization changed. We lack a single operational rubric that ties telemetry -> business action. This causes manual triage, inconsistent customer comms, and slowed fallbacks.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define 10 core signal metrics (availability, p50/p95 token latency by region, quantization mismatch flag, inference errorburst rate, model-variant substitution rate, embedding drift score, routing fallback frequency, token-cost delta, route saturation, and KV-cache hit ratio).
- Inventory existing data sources (console telemetry, edge region logs, provider status pages, third-party model registries, GitHub model releases) and map ownership.
- Draft alert thresholds with severity tiers and suggested remediations.
- One short experiment to validate signal precision using historical incidents (Jan–Mar 2026).
- Runbook for rapid PM + Eng coordination (one-pager).

Out of scope: deep instrumentation work, long-term ML drift models, contract/SLA changes (those are follow-ups).
deliverables: 1) One-page operational brief (PDF) for PM/SEs/GTM 2) Confluence 'cookbook' with metrics and owners 3) Minimal alerting dashboard prototype (Grafana links) 4) Experiment notebook and dataset for signal validation 5) Short roll-forward plan for integrating into Console SLOs
acceptance_criteria:
- Brief reviewed and acknowledged by Runtime Eng lead and Head of GTM
- Dashboard prototype shows signal ingestion for at least two regions (us-west, eu-central) with p95 latency and fallback frequency
- Experiment reproduces at least 3 historical degradation events with >70% precision in signal identifying root cause class (model flavor vs infra)
- Runbook includes owner contact matrix and next-step decision tree
notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) Short signal list vs noisy coverage — we prioritize precision (fewer metrics) to avoid alert fatigue. 2) Store-and-forward telemetry for APAC regions adds latency but reduces false negatives; flagged for engineering cost estimate. 3) We will not create contractual SLA changes in this ticket; instead, produce data to inform future SLA proposals.
risks:
- Signal false positives triggering customer escalations
- Dependence on third-party provider status pages (rate limits / TTLs)
- Engineering bandwidth for dashboard integrations could slip the delivery by one cycle
next_steps: 1) Align with ENG runtime owners on metric instrumentation gaps (by 2026-03-12) 2) Kick off 1-week data pull for historical events (2026-03-13) 3) Prototype dashboard (2026-03-17) 4) Draft brief and circulate for review (2026-03-20)
